summary: Review round 2 的 no-ship 修正。最重要的是 finding 1：h3 在 routing 之前就用 ufo decodePath（decodeURIComponent 語意，只保護 %2F 與 %25）解過 path，所以 getRouterParam 拿到的已經不是 client 送的東西 —— 對 build 出來的 server 實測，/api/arbiter/config/rules/a%3Fb 會變成 routerParam 'config/rules/a' + query {b:''}，proxy 靜靜地對『另一個資源』回了 200；rate%25limit 與 a%23b 則是誤判 404。split 之後再怎麼驗都救不回已經遺失的 bytes，所以改成結構性修法：handler 改讀 event.node.req.originalUrl，自己在第一個 '?' 切開（validateProxyTarget），validateProxyPath 驗的是完全未解碼的原始 wildcard，query 逐 byte 原樣轉發，serializeQuery 整個刪掉。finding 2：被拒絕的 3xx 會留著 live body 佔住上游 socket，現在會先 cancel。另外自己補一個 report 沒提到的繞法：WHATWG parser 不會把 reserved %2F 當分隔符，health/%2F%2E%2E/admin 可以原封不動通過 identity 檢查，但 ASGI 上游解完會落在 /health/../admin —— 加上 %2E 一律拒絕的規則，並用測試證明 parser 真的不動那些輸入。finding 3/4 是測試本身的問題：e2e 對四個控制項完全無感（redirect 拒絕、auth gate、response body pipeline、request body 轉發），現在補齊並加上 scripts/proxy-mutation-check.mjs，逐一從 build 出來的 chunk 刪掉控制項並要求測試失敗，四個全部被殺；port 預約的 race 改成 EADDRINUSE 重試（PORT=0 沒用，Nitro 會當 falsy 然後綁 3000）。

findings.what: ignoreResponseError:true means upstream 4xx/5xx bodies are streamed to the browser verbatim, so an upstream that echoed the API key in an error payload would relay it.
findings.resolution: Accepted, not fixed. Requirement 5 governs this proxy's own error messages, not upstream payloads. Status/body pass-through is deliberate and the UI depends on it (422 detail bodies). The upstream is our own FastAPI service. Buffering every error response to inspect it would give up the streaming the design was chosen for. Documented in spec.md under 'Accepted boundary — upstream error response bodies', with the trigger to revisit (upstream becoming third-party).

findings.what: Redirects were followed automatically; undici keeps custom headers cross-origin, so X-API-Key would reach an upstream-chosen origin.
findings.resolution: Fixed. redirect:'manual' on the upstream fetch; isRedirectStatus() turns any 3xx into 502. Not relayed either — relaying would let the upstream steer the browser. Covered by AC-4.7.

findings.severity_agreed: Minor (defence in depth) — severity claim withdrawn
findings.what: validateProxyPath checked only literal '..', so percent-encoded dot segments were said to pass validation and then be canonicalised by the URL parser.
findings.resolution: Hardened, but the reachability claim is withdrawn after runtime measurement. Nitro/h3 hands the catch-all over already decoded with decodeURI semantics — instrumented against the built server, '/api/arbiter/health/%2e%2e/admin' arrives as routerParam 'health/../admin'. So %2e%2e hit the original literal check as '..' and was already rejected; the bypass existed in the pure function, not through the route. The hardening is kept because Nitro's decoding is not a documented contract and validateProxyPath is a pure function whose callers can change. It now rests on parser identity — decodeURI(new URL(wildcard, base).pathname) must equal '/' + wildcard, origin unchanged — which also catches single-dot segments the literal check never could. Both the original 'accepted residual' note and the first retraction (which called this Critical) are corrected in spec.md.

findings.what: classifyUpstreamError only covers the window up to the upstream response headers; a body that stalls after a 200 is committed cannot become a 504.
findings.resolution: Accepted, with the failure mode improved. Buffering the whole body to keep the option of changing the status would give up streaming and cap response size by memory. What changed: sendStream would have ended the response cleanly, so a truncated body looked like a complete 200; pipeline destroys the response socket on a source error, so the client sees an aborted transfer that $fetch surfaces as a rejection. The 30s AbortSignal still covers the body. Documented in spec.md.

findings.what: h3 1.15's web-stream sendStream path neither honours res.write backpressure nor cancels the upstream stream on client disconnect.
findings.resolution: Fixed. The shell now uses pipeline(Readable.fromWeb(body), event.node.res), which propagates backpressure and destroys the source on disconnect. It also ends the response, setting writableEnded, which is what h3's event.handled getter reads.

findings.what: readRawBody was wrapped in .catch(() => undefined), so an aborted upload became a successful upstream write with an empty body.
findings.resolution: Fixed. A read failure returns 400 Invalid Request Body and the upstream is never called; the detail is logged. Covered by AC-4.5, including a non-Error rejection.

findings.what: The security-critical route was at 0% coverage on all four metrics; global thresholds passed because frontend coverage masked it. The 100% claim covered isolated helpers only.
findings.resolution: Fixed in two layers. (a) The route was split: all policy moved to server/utils/proxyHandler.ts as runProxy(request, deps) with injected getSessionUser / readBody / fetchUpstream / logError, covered by 41 tests at 100/100/100/100 — auth ordering, both gates, header wiring, body handling, redirect refusal, error classification, status sanitisation, and the real (non-injected) timeout-signal default. (b) The remaining h3 shell is covered by tests/e2e/proxy.e2e.test.ts, which spawns the built server plus a mock upstream and drives it over a raw node:http socket, asserting against what the upstream actually received. It runs in CI as its own step after pnpm build. The reviewer's own mutation scenario now fails: deleting the session gate breaks AC-4.1, and deleting the path guards from the built bundle fails 7 of the 8 AC-5.1 cases (verified, then restored).

findings.what: Non-timeout failures returned the raw cause message to the browser; redacting the API key does not stop disclosure of internal hostnames, IPs, ports or TLS details.
findings.resolution: Fixed, and treated as more than Minor since it is an information-disclosure boundary. classifyUpstreamError now returns { statusCode, message, detail }: message is a fixed token ('upstream-timeout' / 'upstream-unreachable') and is the only thing the browser sees; detail carries the redacted cause and goes to stderr only. The test that enshrined the old behaviour was rewritten.

findings.what: The undefined-query test was synthetic: getQuery cannot produce undefined, and useApi.ts strips it before the request, so a route that forwarded 'action=' unchanged would still pass.
findings.resolution: Fixed by adding a real assertion at the route level: AC-5.4 drives GET /api/arbiter/decisions?limit=5 through the built server and asserts the mock upstream received exactly '/decisions?limit=5'. The pure-function test is kept as a unit-level contract for serializeQuery.

retry_history.note: The round-2 agent produced an empty output file and never wrote its report. The report was recovered verbatim from the codex rollout log (payload.last_agent_message) and committed as 52a67ac before any fix was attempted, so the findings below are the reviewer’s own words, not a reconstruction.

findings.what: The handler validated h3’s decoded router parameter, not the request target. h3 runs ufo decodePath (decodeURIComponent semantics, only %2F and %25 protected) on the path half of the raw URL before the router splits it, so an encoded delimiter is gone by the time any check runs.
findings.measured: Against .output/: /api/arbiter/config/rules/a%3Fb -> routerParam "config/rules/a", query {b:""} -> upstream GET /config/rules/a?b= with a 200. /api/arbiter/config/rules/rate%25limit -> "config/rules/rate%limit" -> 404. /api/arbiter/config/rules/a%23b -> "config/rules/a" -> 404.
findings.resolution: Fixed structurally. The shell reads event.node.req.originalUrl (assigned once by h3 before any layer runs, per createAppEventHandler) and validateProxyTarget splits at the first "?" itself. validateProxyPath now takes the raw, undecoded wildcard and only case-canonicalises escapes (%2f -> %2F). serializeQuery and QueryInput are deleted; the query is relayed byte for byte. Covered by AC-6.1 through AC-6.4.

findings.what: A refused upstream redirect returned 502 without cancelling the response body, so the upstream socket stayed occupied until GC or the 30s signal. A redirect loop could drain the connection pool while every request got a prompt 502.
findings.resolution: Fixed. await upstream.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined) before returning. Three tests: cancel is called once and the stream is left unlocked, a rejecting cancel still yields 502, and a bodyless 3xx does not throw. AC-6.6.

findings.what: The e2e suite was vacuous for four shell controls: removing redirect:"manual", making getSessionUser always truthy, replacing the pipeline with res.end(), or making readBody return undefined all left the suite green. Every case was an authenticated GET against an upstream that never redirected and whose body nobody read.
findings.resolution: Fixed, and automated so it cannot regress. The mock upstream now serves a real cross-origin 302 (to a third server that records whether it was ever contacted) and a 512KB body; the suite adds an unauthenticated request, a PUT, a full-body comparison and POST/PATCH/DELETE body relay. scripts/proxy-mutation-check.mjs (pnpm test:e2e:mutation, a CI step after the e2e one) deletes each of the four controls from the built chunk in turn and requires the suite to fail. All four are killed. AC-6.7.

findings.what: reservePort closes its listener before spawning the application, so the port is unreserved for the whole of start-up.
findings.resolution: Fixed as a retry rather than a narrower window: a failed bind is retried on a fresh port up to 5 times, and any other start-up failure is reported with the captured server log. PORT=0 was measured and does not work — Nitro reads it as falsy and binds 3000. AC-6.8.

findings.severity_reported: not in the report — found while fixing #1
findings.what: health/%2F%2E%2E/admin and health/%2F%2E%2E%2Fadmin survive the parser-identity check byte-for-byte, because the WHATWG parser does not treat a reserved %2F as a separator. An upstream that decodes the whole target lands on /health/../admin.
findings.resolution: Fixed by rejecting any %2E outright: a dot never needs encoding inside a path segment, so the escape only ever appears to smuggle a dot segment. Two tests assert the parser really does leave those inputs unchanged, so the rule is shown to be load-bearing rather than redundant with identity. AC-6.5.

behaviour_delta.what: Deleting serializeQuery removes a server-side normalisation of two query shapes that ufo withQuery handles differently: {since: null} serialises to a bare "?since", and {action: ["a", undefined, "b"]} to "?action=a&action=undefined&action=b" (both measured against the installed ufo).
behaviour_delta.why_accepted: Neither reaches the proxy from this codebase: getDecisions filters v != null itself, the remaining callers pass typed optional params, and ofetch drops undefined values client-side. Re-introducing a server-side rewrite of the query is precisely what caused finding 1, so the verbatim relay stands. Recorded in tasks.md under Task 6 rather than dropped silently.

verification.lint_check: pnpm lint:check — 0 errors, 10 warnings (all pre-existing vue/no-static-inline-styles in pages/*.vue, unchanged from base)
verification.test_coverage: pnpm test:coverage — 12 files, 280 tests passed. All files 45.31 lines / 83.33 branches / 59.6 functions / 45.31 statements. server/utils/proxyHandler.ts 100/100/100/100. server/utils/proxyPolicy.ts 98.3/97.36/100/98.3 (uncovered: lines 159-160, the new URL catch, unreachable by construction and kept as a degrade-to-404 guard).
verification.test_e2e: pnpm test:e2e — 1 file, 28 tests passed against the built server (.output/server/index.mjs) plus a mock upstream and a separate redirect-target server, over a raw node:http socket.
verification.test_e2e_mutation: pnpm test:e2e:mutation — M1 redirect:"manual", M2 the session gate, M3 the response-body pipeline and M4 the request-body reader are each deleted from the built shell chunk in turn; the e2e suite fails on all four. M5 (req.url for originalUrl) survives and is asserted to, with the h3 source reason recorded in the script.
verification.coverage_ratchet: No change this round. Measured 45.31/83.33/59.6 gives floor-2 of 43/81/57, which is what vitest.config.ts already holds.
verification.hooks: Both round-2 commits went through husky pre-commit (lint-staged + vitest run --changed). --no-verify was not used.

h3_decodes_the_path_before_routing: h3 1.15.11 createAppEventHandler: originalUrl is assigned once, before any layer runs; _decodePath (ufo decodePath, decodeURIComponent-based with %2F and %25 protected) is applied to the path half of the raw URL; req.url is then reassigned per layer.
request line /api/arbiter/config/rules/a%3Fb        -> routerParam "config/rules/a", query {b:""}  (200 against the WRONG resource)
All three now return 200 with the upstream receiving the path byte-for-byte as sent.
runtime_evidence.why_originalUrl_and_not_req_url: req.url happens to hold the same string today: h3 restores the raw URL whenever decoding changed it and the layer is mounted at "/", which is how Nitro mounts this router. That is measured, not relied on — the mutation check records it as an equivalent mutant (M5) rather than as covered behaviour. originalUrl is used because it is assigned once, before any layer runs, so it also survives a future nested mount.
parser_facts_the_rules_rest_on: The WHATWG serializer upper-cases hex escapes (%3f -> %3F), so escapes are canonicalised before comparison rather than rejected for spelling.
%zz and a bare % pass through the parser unchanged, so identity cannot catch a malformed escape — hence the explicit BAD_ESCAPE rule.
A reserved %2F is not treated as a separator, so health/%2F%2E%2E/admin survives identity byte-for-byte — hence the explicit %2E rule.
runtime_evidence.upstream_headers_observed: user-agent: arbiter-proxy on every hit; cookie never forwarded; x-api-key present on every hit; the redirect target server recorded zero requests.

open_ac.reason: Still requires a manual smoke test of every page against the real backend. This worktree's .env holds only NUXT_SESSION_PASSWORD — no NUXT_API_KEY or NUXT_API_BASE_URL — so it cannot be verified here. Substitute evidence is unchanged: all 26 useApi.ts endpoint paths pass the allowlist, and the new e2e layer now also proves a correctly encoded path with a space reaches the upstream. What remains unverified is real backend behaviour, not proxy routing.

deviations.what: The proxy sets an explicit outgoing User-Agent (PROXY_USER_AGENT = 'arbiter-proxy') rather than sending none.
deviations.why: AC-2.4 asks for no user-agent upstream, but the fetch specification requires the header: when the caller sets none the runtime appends its own default. Pinning a constant makes the value deliberate and testable instead of runtime-dependent. AC-2.4's security intent is fully met.
deviations.impact: None on behaviour. Asserted end to end by AC-5.5.

deviations.what: Traversal probes use a raw node:http socket instead of fetch.
deviations.why: undici's fetch resolves '..' before the request is sent, so a fetch-based probe never reaches the server with the literal path and produced a false 200 on the first run.
deviations.impact: Test methodology only. Now permanent, in tests/e2e/proxy.e2e.test.ts rather than a throwaway script.

deviations.what: WITHDRAWN. The previous handoff recorded an accepted residual — that a percent-encoded '%2e%2e' in a later segment was not rejected, and that this was 'not exploitable'.
deviations.why: The reasoning given for accepting it ('the first-segment allowlist still applies') was wrong on its own terms, which is what review #3 correctly identified. The residual is now closed by the parser-identity check. Note that reachability was also overstated in the other direction by the first retraction — see retry_history codex-3.

deviations.what: A new npm script (test:e2e), a second vitest config (vitest.e2e.config.ts) and a new CI step were added, which are outside the original spec's file list.
deviations.why: Review #7 required the route to be covered by something repeatable that runs in CI. The e2e suite needs a build in .output/ and a node environment, so it cannot share the unit config without slowing every unit run and dragging measured coverage down with a file v8 cannot see into.
deviations.impact: pnpm test and pnpm test:coverage are unchanged in scope and runtime. CI gains one step after Build.

deviations.what: A second new npm script (test:e2e:mutation), a new scripts/ directory and a second CI step were added.
deviations.why: Round-2 finding 3 was that a green e2e run proved nothing for four controls. A committed, runnable mutation check is the only form of that answer that survives the next change to the suite.
deviations.impact: CI gains one step after the e2e one, roughly five e2e runs long (~10s total here). pnpm test and pnpm test:coverage are unchanged.
